acceptedFindings.title: Analysis is ungoverned exploratory and lacks pre-specified protocol
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without a pre-registered protocol, p-values and confidence intervals are not controlled for multiplicity and have no confirmatory value; any claim of association is hypothesis-generating at best.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Either pre-register a full analysis plan and re-run the analysis under that governance, or clearly label results as exploratory and remove p-values and confidence intervals, providing only descriptive summaries and effect sizes with no assertion of 'significance'.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check for existence of bound analysisSpec or methodSelection artifacts; they are null.

acceptedFindings.title: Variable definitions, units, and coding are absent
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Interpretation of odds ratios is impossible without knowing what outcome_binary=1 means, how treatment is coded, what severity and albumin measure and their units.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide a comprehensive codebook: define each variable, its possible values, units, and any transformations. Include this in the manuscript or a supplementary artifact.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Search for variable definitions in manuscript or companion artifact; none found.

acceptedFindings.title: Omitted covariate 'albumin' from results
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The model included albumin as a covariate (as per stats-run.json), but the manuscript fails to report its coefficient, odds ratio, confidence interval, or p-value. This omission prevents readers from assessing the full model and could indicate selective reporting.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add the albumin results to the manuscript's results section and discuss its role in adjustment. If albumin was excluded from the final model, justify the model reduction and report it transparently.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Compare estimates list in stats-run.json (which contains an 'albumin' term) with the manuscript's results section (which lists only const, treatment, age, severity). Albumin is present in the model outputs but absent from the manuscript.

acceptedFindings.title: Inappropriate normality test applied to logistic regression residuals
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The Shapiro-Wilk test (p=5.6e-8) is applied to logistic regression residuals, which do not assume normality. This indicates a fundamental misunderstanding of the model class and may mask more relevant diagnostics.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Replace the Shapiro-Wilk test with appropriate logistic regression diagnostics such as Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit, calibration plots, or discrimination metrics. Remove misleading normality p-values.

acceptedFindings.title: Cohort assembly and missingness process not described
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Selection bias from missing data or eligibility criteria can distort associations; without reporting the flow from source to analytic sample, risk of bias is unclear.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the number of observations excluded at each step, reasons for missingness, and compare characteristics of included vs excluded subjects. Conduct sensitivity analysis for missing data (e.g., multiple imputation if applicable).
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: No cohort flow diagram or missingness table in artifacts.

acceptedFindings.title: Model diagnostics are insufficient and partly inappropriate
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Logistic regression residuals are not normally distributed; Shapiro-Wilk test is meaningless. Also, no separation check (e.g., Firth's bias correction, profile likelihood confidence intervals) is reported, which is critical for sparse outcomes or small samples. Cook's distance max 0.045 is noted but not interpreted.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Remove Shapiro-Wilk test. Report a separation diagnostic (e.g., check for complete or quasi-separation using the R separatedetect package or similar). If separation is possible, use Firth penalized logistic regression. For influence, highlight any observations with Cook's distance > 0.5 or leverage > 2p/n.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Shapiro p-value present in diagnostics; no separation diagnostic field.

acceptedFindings.title: Causal language used without causal framework
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Phrases like 'treatment associated ... after adjustment' imply a causal interpretation, but no DAG or confounder selection rationale is provided. Observational studies require explicit causal assumptions and sensitivity analyses to move beyond association.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Either adopt causal language strictly, e.g., 'estimated association', or provide a DAG and justify covariate selection. Include a sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding (e.g., E-value).
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: No causal diagram or confounder selection justification found.

acceptedFindings.title: Exploratory posture mismatch with manuscript claims
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The stats-run.json explicitly marks the result as 'exploratory_standard_table' and states it cannot support 'paper-ready conclusions' or 'causal claims'. The manuscript presents the analysis as a definitive local study, overreaching the evidence level.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Either downgrade the manuscript's conclusions to explicitly match the exploratory posture, or provide a bound analysis specification and rerun the analysis to upgrade the posture before presenting it as a final study.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check resultPosture.cannotSupport in stats-run.json: it lists 'paper-ready conclusions' and 'causal claims'. The manuscript's Discussion and Conclusion imply applicability beyond exploration.

acceptedFindings.title: Implausible negative BIC value
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The BIC is reported as -1032.88. For logistic regression with moderate sample size, BIC should be positive (e.g., around AIC+log(n)*k). A negative BIC suggests a computational error or a mislabelled statistic, undermining trust in the entire model output.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Verify the BIC calculation against standard formulas (e.g., BIC = -2*logLik + log(n)*k). If corrected, update the diagnostics and manuscript. If the negative value persists, document the formula used and explain the discrepancy.

acceptedFindings.title: Missing separation diagnostic evidence
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md Limitations: 'explicit separation diagnostic evidence was not found'
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Logistic regression is prone to separation, especially with sparse data or multiple predictors. Without evidence that separation was checked (e.g., large standard errors, infinite estimates, or Firth's method), the validity of parameter estimates is uncertain.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Perform separation diagnostics: inspect for large coefficient variances, add a penalized likelihood option, or report confidence intervals for odds ratios that are finite and plausible. Include these results in the manuscript.

acceptedFindings.title: Outcome prevalence not reported
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without outcome prevalence, the intercept odds and baseline risk are not interpretable. This also affects evaluation of model calibration.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the number and proportion of outcome=1 in the cohort.

acceptedFindings.title: Manuscript self-referentially claims no reader-facing paper artifact
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The limitation 'No reader-facing paper/manuscript artifact was found' is confusing given that this manuscript is that artifact; it appears to be a template leftover. This reduces clarity.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Remove or clarify this line; if it refers to an external reader-facing report, specify that.

acceptedFindings.title: Incomplete model specification in manuscript
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript states the primary outcome, exposure, and covariates were not fully encoded in the text report. For reproducibility, a clear declaration of all variables and model form (e.g., logistic regression of outcome_binary ~ treatment + age + severity + albumin) is essential.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Explicitly list all variables included in the final model and the regression formula within the Methods section.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: The variables section lacks the model formula; compare with stats-run.json variables array which lists outcome_binary, treatment, age, severity, albumin.

acceptedFindings.title: No raw data or data dictionary provided
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Full reproducibility requires access to de-identified data or at least summary statistics. The manuscript mentions artifact inventory but does not include a public data statement.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: If data cannot be shared, provide a detailed data dictionary and summary statistics of all variables. Specify access conditions.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: No data file or data dictionary artifact in provided list.
